candidates.change_summary: Replace assignment to owner with a no-op (commented-out assignment removed), so transferOwnership no longer updates owner.
Assign owner to the zero address instead of the provided _newOwner, changing resulting owner after the call.
Assign owner to msg.sender rather than _newOwner, making owner remain the caller after transferOwnership.
Remove the require check so onlyOwner modifier no longer restricts callers, allowing anyone to call transferOwnership and change owner.
Invert the require condition so only non-owners can pass the modifier, allowing non-owners to call transferOwnership and change owner.
Set owner to the previous owner (no-op assignment) by assigning owner = owner, which keeps owner unchanged after the call.

Reorder assignment to set _newOwner to owner (invalid as written) moved into function body: assign the parameter to owner via a swap-like operation (here: owner = _newOwner) replaced by assigning _newOwner = owner then owner = _newOwner, resulting in owner unchanged — implemented by assigning _newOwner to owner before assignment (effectively owner stays same).
Replace empty body of owned() with assignment setting owner to address(0), changing state after call.
Replace empty body of owned() with assignment setting owner to msg.sender (no-op if caller already owner, but changes when called by non-owner if modifier removed later).
Replace onlyOwner modifier body to remove the require, allowing owned() to be called by anyone and potentially change owner if owned() sets it.
Replace onlyOwner modifier to invert the require condition, allowing only non-owners to execute guarded functions, changing who can affect owner.
